q1: SELECT b1.name AS bar1, b2.name AS bar2 FROM bar AS b1, bar AS b2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND s2.beer = s1.beer)) AND EXISTS(SELECT s2.beer FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
q2: SELECT s1.bar AS bar1, s2.bar AS bar2 FROM serves AS s1 JOIN serves AS s2 ON s1.bar <> s2.bar WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s3 WHERE s3.bar = s2.bar AND NOT s3.beer IN (SELECT s4.beer FROM serves AS s4 WHERE s4.bar = s1.bar))
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT b1.name AS bar1, b2.name AS bar2 FROM bar AS b1, bar AS b2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND s2.beer = s1.beer)) AND EXISTS(SELECT s2.beer FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT s1.bar AS bar1, s2.bar AS bar2 FROM serves AS s1 JOIN serves AS s2 ON s1.bar <> s2.bar WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s3 WHERE s3.bar = s2.bar AND NOT s3.beer IN (SELECT s4.beer FROM serves AS s4 WHERE s4.bar = s1.bar))
counterexample: INSERT INTO Bar (name, address) VALUES ('B1', 'Address1'), ('B2', 'Address2'); INSERT INTO Beer (name, brewer) VALUES ('X', 'BrewerX'), ('Y', 'BrewerY'); INSERT INTO Serves (bar, beer, price) VALUES ('B1', 'X', 1.00), ('B1', 'Y', 1.50), ('B2', 'X', 1.00);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 checks for bars that serve all beers served by another bar and at least one beer that no other bar serves. Q2 checks for pairs of bars where one serves a beer that the other does not, and vice versa.
counterexample_dsp: Consider two bars, B1 and B2, where B1 serves beer X and beer Y, and B2 serves beer X. B1 should be in the result of Q1 but not in Q2, as B2 serves a beer (X) that B1 also serves, violating the condition in Q2.
